statements.t: The Company intends to pursue both selective ownership and management of real estate assets and fee-based technology and administration services for third-party property owners and operators.

Under this model, TAP Real Estate intends to acquire, hold, operate, and manage select real estate assets while utilizing the licensed TAP technology infrastructure to support property administration, digital recordkeeping, investor onboarding, tokenization, compliant issuance, distributions, and lifecycle management.

For each potential transaction, the Company expects to define the issuer, investor rights, authoritative ownership records, offering path, transfer controls, and ongoing servicing before any token issuance.

TAP Real Estate plans to drive revenues through a blend of management fees, listing fees and success fees on tokenized listings of real estate listings; as well as adding to the balance-sheet value any properties that are attributed to the TAP Real Estate portfolio after vetting by the TAP Real Estate team.
We expect our professional fees to increase in our next 12 months as we look to scale our TAP Real Estate Technologies business.
We expect that these costs will increase during the later part of 2026 into 2027.

The consolidated financial statements of the Company have been prepared assuming that the Company will continue as a going concern, which contemplates, among other things, the realization of assets and the satisfaction of liabilities in the normal course of business over a reasonable period.

dropped.t: The Company intends to keep a portion of the HoldCo Units to maintain exposure to WSCG’s performance and the Company assets purchased by WSCG.

As a result of the WSCG purchase of the Company assets, the previous operations of the Company will be reflected as discontinued operations, and the assets that were sold are all reflected as assets under discontinued operations.
We expect our professional fees to continue to decrease in our next 12 months as we look to scale back on outside contract labor due to the change in our business operations.
We expect that these costs will continue decreasing during 2025.
The Company anticipates entering into profitable businesses upon the sale of the magnesium silicate.
The Company does not discuss recent pronouncements that are not anticipated to have an impact on or are unrelated to its financial condition, results of operations, cash flows or disclosures.

estimates.name: Fair Value of Financial Instruments
estimates.t: ASC 825 Financial Instruments requires the Company to disclose estimated fair values for its financial instruments.

estimates.name: Fair Value Measurements
estimates.t: Level 2 inputs: Quoted prices for similar instruments in active markets; quoted prices for identical or similar instruments in markets that are not active; and model-derived valuations whose inputs are observable or whose significant value drivers are observable.

estimates.name: Non-Equity Method Equity Securities
estimates.t: These investments consist of equity interests in privately held entities over which the Company does not have a controlling financial interest or significant influence.

estimates.name: Equity Method Investments
estimates.t: The Company accounts for investments in entities over which it has significant influence, but not control or joint control, using the equity method of accounting under ASC 323.

estimates.name: Revenue Recognition
estimates.t: The Company applies the ASC 606 five-step model: Contracts generally do not include variable consideration; if present, it is estimated and included only if a significant reversal is not probable.
